# package gdsserver

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/gds/gdsserver"
```

Package gdsserver makes a server.Server a Global Discovery Server (GDS) by the pull model of OPC UA Part 12 (v1.05): the Directory object with the application directory (§6: RegisterApplication, UpdateApplication, UnregisterApplication, FindApplications, GetApplication, QueryApplications, QueryServers) and certificate management (§7.9: StartSigningRequest, StartNewKeyPairRequest, FinishRequest, RevokeCertificate, GetCertificateGroups, GetCertificates, GetTrustList, GetCertificateStatus, CheckRevocationStatus) with the TrustLists of its certificate groups.

Attach imports the GDS information model (namespace [http://opcfoundation.org/UA/GDS/](http://opcfoundation.org/UA/GDS/), node ids of package gdsid) into a server before it starts. The GDS signs certificates with its own certificate authorities, one per key type (RSA, NIST P-256, NIST P-384, brainpoolP256r1, brainpoolP384r1, Ed25519, Ed448), issues their CRLs and publishes them in the trust lists. The CAs are generated on first use or configured with Config.Issuers. The state lives in a Store: MemoryStore by default, or NewFileStore for a directory (one JSON file per record, written atomically, private files).

#### Certificate groups {#hdr-Certificate_groups}

  - DefaultApplicationGroup: the application certificate types of Config.CertificateTypes; its trust list holds every CA of the GDS.
  - DefaultHttpsGroup: HttpsCertificateType (TLS server certificates, RSA or ECDSA on P-256 or P-384) when the GDS has an RSA, NistP256 or NistP384 CA; its trust list holds those CAs. A request for it may leave out the ApplicationUri.
  - DefaultUserTokenGroup: issues no certificates; its trust list holds what a CertificateAuthorityAdmin adds (the issuers of the X.509 user tokens a server accepts).

GetCertificateGroups returns the application group for a client and all three (the HTTPS group only if it issues) for a server.

#### Authorization {#hdr-Authorization}

Part 12 §6.2 and §7.2 define who may call what, which the GDS enforces:

  - RegisterApplication needs the DiscoveryAdmin role.
  - UpdateApplication and UnregisterApplication need DiscoveryAdmin or the application itself.
  - GetApplication needs an authenticated user, an administrator or the application itself.
  - FindApplications, QueryApplications and QueryServers are open to every session.
  - StartSigningRequest, StartNewKeyPairRequest and FinishRequest need the CertificateAuthorityAdmin role or the application itself over a SignAndEncrypt channel.
  - RevokeCertificate needs CertificateAuthorityAdmin.
  - GetCertificateGroups, GetCertificates, GetTrustList and GetCertificateStatus need CertificateAuthorityAdmin or the application itself.
  - CheckRevocationStatus is open to every session on a signed channel.
  - The TrustLists may be read by CertificateAuthorityAdmin, SecurityAdmin and the registered applications, and changed by CertificateAuthorityAdmin over SignAndEncrypt.

Every method except FindApplications, GetApplication, QueryApplications and QueryServers needs a signed channel. The roles DiscoveryAdmin and CertificateAuthorityAdmin are nodes of the GDS namespace (GDS.DiscoveryAdminRole, GDS.CertificateAuthorityAdminRole); a server.WithRoleMapper gives them to sessions.

The methods carry the RolePermissions of the GDS NodeSet, which the GDS honours besides the rules above: a session none of whose roles has the Call permission is refused, except for the methods an application calls for itself (ApplicationSelfAdmin is a privilege, not a role). The server.RBACAccessController applies the same RolePermissions before the GDS sees a call and has no notion of the application itself: with it, an application without a role cannot call those methods for itself.

"The application itself" is a session whose channel certificate carries the ApplicationUri of the record and is a certificate the GDS issued to the application and did not revoke. An application that has no such certificate yet, typically one with a self-signed certificate that asks for its first one, is accepted only when Config.SelfAdmin says so; otherwise a CertificateAuthorityAdmin requests the first certificate for it.

#### Certificate requests {#hdr-Certificate_requests}

A request waits for approval (GDS.Requests, GDS.ApproveRequest) unless Config.AutoApprove is set; FinishRequest returns Bad\_NothingToDo while it waits and issues the certificate once it is approved. A signing request must carry the ApplicationUri of the application and a key of the certificate type, of any key type (uapolicy parses and checks the request); the issued certificate gets the host names of the discovery URLs as they are when the request is made (Request.DomainNames, shown by GDS.Requests): a later UpdateApplication does not change them, and a wildcard host is refused with Bad\_InvalidArgument. The private key of StartNewKeyPairRequest is returned as PEM (PKCS #8, encrypted with PBES2 when a password is given) or PFX (PKCS #12 with the certificate and its issuer, protected with the password).

#### Audit events {#hdr-Audit_events}

When the server audits (server.WithAuditing), the methods report the audit events of the GDS NodeSet to the Server object and the Directory: ApplicationRegistrationChangedAuditEventType (Register, Update, Unregister), CertificateRequestedAuditEventType (StartSigningRequest, StartNewKeyPairRequest), CertificateDeliveredAuditEventType (FinishRequest, except while the request waits) and CertificateRevokedAuditEventType, with the arguments but without the password and the private key. A server.EventAccessController (the RBACAccessController: ReceiveEvents for SecurityAdmin, by the NodeSet) decides who receives them.

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Store persists the state (nil: a new MemoryStore).
	Store Store

	// CertificateTypes are the certificate types the
	// DefaultApplicationGroup issues (nil: DefaultCertificateTypes). The
	// first one is used when a request names none.
	CertificateTypes []*ua.NodeID

	// Issuers are certificate authorities to use instead of generating
	// them: Issuer.Name selects the key type ("RSA", "NistP256",
	// "NistP384", "Curve25519", "Curve448"), Certificate and PrivateKey
	// are required, the rest is ignored. An issuer given here replaces the
	// one of the Store, whose revocations it keeps only if it is the same
	// certificate. A CA the GDS needs and neither Issuers nor the Store
	// have is generated and stored.
	Issuers []*Issuer

	// CAName is the common name of the CAs the GDS generates, followed by
	// the key type (default "go-opcua GDS CA").
	CAName string

	// CALifetime, CertificateLifetime and CRLLifetime are the validity of
	// a generated CA, of an issued certificate (at most until the CA
	// expires) and the time from one CRL to its NextUpdate.
	CALifetime          time.Duration
	CertificateLifetime time.Duration
	CRLLifetime         time.Duration

	// RSAKeySize is the size of the RSA keys of StartNewKeyPairRequest
	// (default 2048). A generated RSA CA has 3072 bits.
	RSAKeySize int

	// AutoApprove approves every certificate request when it is made. By
	// default a request waits until GDS.ApproveRequest approves or rejects
	// it, and FinishRequest returns Bad_NothingToDo until then.
	AutoApprove bool

	// RequestLifetime is how long a request that FinishRequest did not
	// complete is kept (default 24 h).
	RequestLifetime time.Duration

	// MaxRequests bounds the open requests of one application (default
	// 8), MaxApplications the registered applications (default 10000).
	MaxRequests     int
	MaxApplications int

	// SelfAdmin decides whether the application whose record is given may
	// manage itself (the ApplicationSelfAdmin privilege of Part 12 §6.2)
	// when it connects with cert, a certificate whose application URI is
	// that of the record but that the GDS did not issue — typically the
	// self-signed certificate of an application that asks for its first
	// certificate. nil allows only the certificates the GDS issued to the
	// application and did not revoke.
	SelfAdmin func(app *gds.ApplicationRecord, cert *x509.Certificate) bool

	// Now returns the current time (nil: time.Now).
	Now func() time.Time

	// Logger receives the log of the GDS (nil: slog.Default()).
	Logger *slog.Logger
}
```

### type FileStore

```go
type FileStore struct {
	// contains filtered or unexported fields
}
```

FileStore is a Store that keeps the state in a directory, one JSON file per application, request and certificate authority and one for the Meta:

	<dir>/applications/<id>.json
	<dir>/requests/<id>.json
	<dir>/issuers/<name>.json
	<dir>/meta.json

Every file is written to a temporary file in its directory, synced and renamed over the old one, so a crash leaves the old or the new version. The files hold the private keys of the CAs and the passwords of pending new key pair requests: they are created with mode 0600 and the directories with 0700. A FileStore may be used by one GDS at a time.

GDS is a Global Discovery Server (OPC UA Part 12 §6 and §7.9, the pull model): the Directory object, an instance of the CertificateDirectoryType, on a server.Server.

#### func Attach

```go
func Attach(srv *server.Server, cfg Config) (*GDS, error)
```

Attach makes srv a GDS: it imports the GDS information model (namespace gdsid.NamespaceURI, which it adds to srv) with the Directory object, loads the state from cfg.Store and serves the methods of the Directory and the TrustLists of its certificate groups. Call it once, before srv.Start.

The GDS namespace gets the next free namespace index: 1 when Attach is the first to add a namespace to srv. The roles of Part 12 §6.2 are in that namespace; give them to sessions with server.WithRoleMapper, see GDS.DiscoveryAdminRole and GDS.CertificateAuthorityAdminRole.

The methods need a session over a secured channel; srv should offer SignAndEncrypt endpoints and validate client certificates.

#### func (GDS) ApproveRequest

```go
func (g *GDS) ApproveRequest(ctx context.Context, requestID string, approve bool) error
```

ApproveRequest approves (approve true) or rejects a pending certificate request by its ID (the GUID of the RequestId). The CertificateAuthority of an application decides with it when Config.AutoApprove is not set.


CertificateAuthorityAdminRole returns the NodeId of the CertificateAuthorityAdmin role of Part 12 §7.2: a session with it may request, revoke and read the certificates of every application and change the trust list.

#### func (GDS) Close

```go
func (g *GDS) Close()
```

Close stops the GDS: its methods return Bad\_ShutDown from then on, and Close returns when the calls in progress completed. The GDS then no longer writes to its Store, which another GDS may take over. Close the server separately.

### type Store

```go
type Store interface {
	// Load returns the complete state, the zero State for a new store.
	Load(ctx context.Context) (*State, error)

	// PutApplication inserts or replaces the application with its ID.
	PutApplication(ctx context.Context, app *Application) error
	// DeleteApplication removes the application with the ID.
	DeleteApplication(ctx context.Context, id string) error

	// PutRequest inserts or replaces the request with its ID.
	PutRequest(ctx context.Context, req *Request) error
	// DeleteRequest removes the request with the ID.
	DeleteRequest(ctx context.Context, id string) error

	// PutIssuer inserts or replaces the certificate authority with its
	// Name.
	PutIssuer(ctx context.Context, iss *Issuer) error

	// PutMeta replaces the counters and the trust list additions.
	PutMeta(ctx context.Context, meta *Meta) error
}
```

Store persists the state of a GDS: the application directory, the certificate requests, the certificate authorities and the trust list.

The GDS reads the whole state when it is attached to a server and keeps it in memory; it then writes every change through to the Store before the change takes effect. A failing write fails the method call with Bad\_InternalError and leaves the state as it was. Only one GDS may use a Store at a time.

A Store holds secrets: the private keys of the certificate authorities (Issuer.PrivateKey) and the passwords of pending new key pair requests (Request.PrivateKeyPassword). A persistent implementation must protect them.

The values passed to a Store and returned by it are not shared with the GDS afterwards: an implementation may keep them as they are, and must not change them.
